paragraphs: Neural language models can produce repetitive, unnatural text when decoding favors the most likely continuation. Adding randomness or discouraging particular tokens can reduce repetition, but the resulting text may lose coherence. This paper investigates the model’s internal token representations as an underlying contributor to that problem.

The authors identify an anisotropic representation space: token representations are distributed unevenly across directions. Their proposed framework addresses both training and generation. SimCTG is a contrastive training objective intended to calibrate that space. Contrastive search is a decoding method designed to encourage varied text while preserving a coherent continuation. Together, these components connect the organization of internal representations to the choices made when producing text.

Experiments and analyses cover three benchmarks in two languages. The authors report improvements over state-of-the-art generation methods according to both human assessments and automatic metrics. These findings support addressing representation geometry alongside decoding, rather than treating unwanted repetition only as a problem of which token to select next.
neurips-2022-a-contrastive-framework-for.tldr: SimCTG and contrastive search jointly address token representations and decoding to improve text diversity while maintaining coherence.

paragraphs: A sampling-based account of perception proposes that fluctuating neural responses represent samples from a posterior distribution over possible stimuli. This raises a timing problem: sampling must be fast enough to explain rapid brain computation. The paper studies a possible acceleration mechanism in continuous attractor neural networks, a canonical model of neural circuits.

The authors introduce noisy adaptation into the network’s neuronal dynamics. Their theoretical derivation connects the resulting process to Hamiltonian dynamics with friction, an efficient sampling method. In this connection, noisy adaptation acts like momentum. The analysis therefore gives a computational interpretation to a feature of the neural dynamics, linking it to faster sampling of latent continuous variables.

The paper analyzes sampling performance and derives a condition under which acceleration is greatest. Simulations support those theoretical results. Extending the model to coupled networks also accelerates sampling for multivariate stimuli. The contribution is a theoretically supported circuit mechanism that could help explain efficient Bayesian inference, demonstrated within the studied network models.
neurips-2022-adaptation-accelerating-sam.tldr: Noisy adaptation accelerates sampling in continuous attractor neural networks by playing a momentum-like role.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to learn an energy-based prior in a generator’s latent space. Such a prior determines which hidden representations the generator favors. Learning it typically involves costly Markov chain Monte Carlo computations. The authors instead investigate noise contrastive estimation, which learns through a discriminative density-ratio estimation problem.

The central obstacle is that estimating the ratio between the latent prior and posterior becomes unreliable when those distributions are far apart. The proposed method divides that task into several adaptive stages. Each stage estimates a ratio and uses the previous stage’s estimate to progressively update the prior. The final energy-based prior is formed through the product of the ratios learned across stages.

This staged construction makes a large distributional gap manageable through successive estimation problems. The authors report efficient training and priors that are more informative and substantially sharper than existing baselines. Experiments show strong performance in image generation, image reconstruction, and anomaly detection, connecting the improved latent prior to several uses of the generator.
neurips-2022-adaptive-multi-stage-densit.tldr: Adaptive density-ratio estimation learns a latent energy-based prior through successive updates that bridge a difficult prior–posterior gap.

paragraphs: Thompson sampling uses uncertainty over model parameters to guide decisions. Maintaining the exact posterior distribution can be computationally impractical, motivating ensemble sampling as an approximation. This paper asks whether that practical substitute can receive a rigorous performance guarantee, focusing on the linear bandit problem.

The main result is a regret bound for ensemble sampling in that setting. Regret measures the cost of decisions relative to an appropriate optimal reference, so bounding it provides a way to assess the quality of sequential choices. The abstract describes the bound as ensuring desirable behavior and identifies this as the first rigorous regret analysis of ensemble sampling.

The proof draws on information-theoretic concepts and new analytical techniques. Its significance is that a computationally motivated approximation now has formal support in the studied decision problem. The authors also suggest that the analytical tools may be useful beyond this paper. That broader usefulness is presented as a possibility; the stated guarantee concerns ensemble sampling for linear bandits.
neurips-2022-an-analysis-of-ensemble-sam.tldr: The paper provides the first rigorous regret analysis of ensemble sampling, establishing a guarantee for linear bandits.

paragraphs: Generating gestures from speech often means predicting a skeleton or a set of body keypoints. This paper studies generating a sequence of speaker images directly from speech audio. The goal is to produce visible gestures in video, addressing a problem relevant to human-machine interaction and digital entertainment.

The proposed framework, ANGIE, separates gestures into reusable motion patterns and finer movements associated with speech rhythm. It learns an unsupervised motion representation instead of imposing a structural body representation such as a two-dimensional skeleton. A vector-quantized motion extractor gathers common gesture patterns into codebooks, giving the system a collection of reusable motion elements.

A second component, Co-Speech GPT with motion refinement, supplies subtle movement details connected to speech prosody. This division lets the framework represent both recurring gesture structure and fine rhythmic variation. The authors report that extensive experiments produce realistic, vivid gesture videos. The stated finding supports combining these two levels of motion within a unified image-generation framework.
neurips-2022-audio-driven-co-speech-gest.tldr: ANGIE generates gesture videos from speech by combining reusable motion patterns with fine rhythmic movement.

paragraphs: The paper studies a platform that pays privacy-conscious users for data to estimate a population mean. Users care about two distinct exposures: sharing information with the platform and the platform publishing its estimate. Their sensitivities to these local and central privacy losses differ, and the platform does not know each person’s sensitivities.

The mechanism must elicit users’ preferences, compensate their privacy losses, and provide both privacy guarantees. Its objective combines estimation error with expected payments. The authors first establish minimax lower bounds on estimation error for given privacy guarantees, then show that a linear estimator is optimal or nearly optimal. This links the statistical accuracy problem to the acquisition problem.

For mechanism design, the Bayesian assumption is that the platform knows the distribution of privacy sensitivities, though not their individual realizations. Under this setting, the authors formulate the design problem as nonconvex optimization. Within the class of linear estimators, they prove that an optimal mechanism can be approximated using a polynomial-time approximation scheme.
neurips-2022-bridging-central-and-local-.tldr: The paper designs data-purchasing mechanisms that balance estimation error, payments, and users’ local and central privacy preferences.

paragraphs: Concept bottleneck models make predictions through intermediate concepts that people can understand and correct. This creates a useful interaction: fixing a mistaken concept can improve the final prediction. Existing approaches, however, struggle to combine accurate predictions, meaningful explanations, and effective corrections, especially when concept annotations are incomplete.

Concept Embedding Models replace a restrictive concept representation with interpretable, high-dimensional representations. The aim is to retain the human-facing concept layer while allowing it to carry richer information. In the reported experiments, these representations capture meaningful semantics both within and beyond the supplied concept labels, helping explain why the concept layer need not force a large accuracy sacrifice.

The authors report task accuracy that matches or exceeds standard neural models without concepts. Human-style concept interventions at test time improve accuracy more than in standard concept bottleneck models. The models also scale to settings where complete concept supervision is scarce. Together, these findings support richer concept representations as a way to improve prediction and intervention within the same model.
neurips-2022-concept-embedding-models-be.tldr: Concept Embedding Models use richer interpretable concept representations to support accurate predictions and more effective concept corrections.

paragraphs: A foundation model can perform well on average while failing badly for a particular group. Across nine robustness benchmarks, this paper finds gaps of up to 80.7 percentage points between average and worst-group accuracy in zero-shot classification. Lightweight adapters do not consistently solve the problem and sometimes make group robustness worse.

The authors observe that examples from different groups within the same class can lie far apart in the model’s embedding space. Ordinary adapter training may leave that separation intact. Their contrastive adapting strategy trains adapters to bring examples closer to both their correct class embeddings and other examples belonging to the same class.

Across the nine benchmarks, worst-group accuracy improves by 8.5 to 56.0 percentage points over zero-shot classification. Training uses fixed foundation-model embeddings without fine-tuning the foundation model. On Waterbirds and CelebA, the approach achieves worst-group accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art methods while training less than one percent of model parameters. These results connect a targeted representation adjustment to efficient improvements for disadvantaged groups.
neurips-2022-contrastive-adapters-for-fo.tldr: Contrastively trained adapters improve worst-group accuracy by aligning same-class embeddings without fine-tuning the foundation model.

paragraphs: A language model can access external knowledge by retrieving relevant context from a database. This reduces the need to store large amounts of world knowledge in its parameters. The paper studies a simple architecture for incorporating that context, motivated by the parameter efficiency, interpretability, and modularity of retrieval-augmented modeling.

The architecture uses a decoupled encoder–decoder arrangement. Its central design choice is to separate context processing within this structure while still making retrieved information available for language modeling. This makes the paper’s question concrete: how effectively can a straightforward architectural arrangement connect external context to the model’s predictions?

The authors report competitive results on autoregressive language modeling and open-domain question answering. They also analyze model behavior described as grounded context transfer and discuss the computational implications of retrieval augmentation. The contribution is evidence that a simple decoupled architecture can work competitively across these tasks, alongside an examination of how it uses context and what that design means computationally.
neurips-2022-decoupled-context-processin.tldr: A simple decoupled encoder–decoder architecture incorporates retrieved context with competitive language-modeling and question-answering results.

paragraphs: One-shot federated learning aims to build a global model using a single communication round between clients and a central server. That saves communication, but existing methods can require public data, matching client architectures, or additional uploaded information. DENSE addresses these practical constraints while preserving the single-round setting.

The framework has two stages: data generation followed by model distillation. Generated data supports the process of transferring information from client models into the global model. Clients transfer model parameters without additional data or model information, and training requires no auxiliary dataset. The framework also accommodates clients whose models have different architectures.

These properties matter because they reduce the coordination and shared-resource requirements of combining separately trained models. Experiments on several real-world datasets favor DENSE over the compared methods. As a concrete example, the authors report a 5.08% improvement over Fed-ADI on CIFAR10. The results support the proposed generation-and-distillation pipeline as a practical approach to the constraints studied in one-shot federated learning.
neurips-2022-dense-data-free-one-shot-fe.tldr: DENSE combines heterogeneous client models in one communication round using data generation and distillation without an auxiliary dataset.

paragraphs: Small connected devices have limited working memory, storage, and computation, making deep convolutional networks difficult to deploy. A common design process first creates a small architecture and then compresses it using different numerical precisions across layers. This paper argues that separating those decisions prevents their joint optimization.

The proposed method chooses the architecture and layer precisions together through an entropy-maximization formulation. Entropy serves as the measure of representation capacity, which the search maximizes subject to a computational budget. The resulting design therefore balances the network’s structure with the precision assigned to each layer within a single automated process.

The design loop runs on a CPU without requiring a GPU, and the authors report searching for an expressive tiny architecture in less than half a CPU hour. Experiments on ImageNet, VWW, and WIDER FACE achieve reported state-of-the-art performance in the tiny-model setting. These results support jointly allocating structural and numerical resources when designing models for constrained devices.
neurips-2022-entropy-driven-mixed-precis.tldr: An entropy-based search jointly selects tiny network architectures and layer precisions under a computational budget.

paragraphs: Autoencoders compress data into a low-dimensional latent representation, but the meaning of that representation can be difficult to interpret without supervision. This paper introduces latent responses, a framework for investigating the structure learned by an autoencoder through interventions on its latent variables.

The approach uses the locally contractive behavior of variational autoencoders to explore the learned data manifold. Its tools actively perturb latent representations and quantify relationships among their variables. This provides a way to examine how the representation responds to changes, giving the analysis a causal focus rather than relying only on associations observed among latent coordinates.

The authors also extend disentanglement to account for the learned generative process. This addresses limitations of existing metrics that may depend on spurious correlations. Their analyses emphasize the importance of causal structure for downstream generation, interpolation, and inference of underlying factors of variation. The contribution is a framework for probing learned representations and a broader way to judge whether their components are meaningfully separated.
neurips-2022-exploring-the-latent-space-.tldr: Latent responses use interventions to probe autoencoder representations and assess disentanglement through the learned generative process.

paragraphs: This paper studies reducing classifier bias by modifying predictions after a black-box model produces them. The proposed wrapper is a learned function called an alpha-tree. This places the intervention at the prediction stage, making the wrapper the object of learning rather than requiring access to the classifier’s internal structure.

The framework builds on an analysis of improper loss functions that can correct distortions in predictions through optimization. Unfairness is treated as such a distortion. The authors provide two general boosting algorithms for learning alpha-trees, giving the conceptual approach concrete training procedures for constructing the prediction adjustment.

The paper establishes properties concerning how alpha-trees compose, generalize, and support interpretation, as well as the KL divergence between original and modified predictions. It illustrates the framework using conditional value-at-risk, equality of opportunity, and statistical parity, with experiments on several available datasets. The contribution is a family of post-processing methods with analytical properties and applications across these three fairness notions.
neurips-2022-fair-wrapping-for-black-box.tldr: Learned alpha-tree wrappers adjust black-box classifier predictions to reduce bias under several fairness notions.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning a large pretrained language model on a limited dataset can cause overfitting and degrade representations acquired during pretraining. The paper addresses how to adapt the model while preserving useful general contextual features. Its method, Dynamic Parameter Selection, changes which parameters receive updates during fine-tuning.

DPS uses gradients from backpropagation to select a promising subnetwork adaptively and update it in stages. The selection is therefore guided by the ongoing optimization process. This makes the choice of what to update part of fine-tuning itself, allowing adaptation to focus on selected portions of a large pretrained model.

On GLUE, the authors report better overall performance and stability than previous fine-tuning methods, with improvements across different pretrained language models. They also report substantial gains in low-resource settings and transfer outside the training domain. These findings support their interpretation that DPS helps retain general contextual features and reduces representation collapse, connecting selective updates to more stable adaptation when target data are limited.
neurips-2022-fine-tuning-pre-trained-lan.tldr: Dynamic Parameter Selection uses gradients to adaptively update subnetworks, improving fine-tuning performance and stability in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Learning directly from complete language instructions can create generalization difficulties for policies acting in complex environments. LISA addresses this by learning intermediate skills from demonstrations paired with language. Its goal is to turn complex instructions into reusable components that can support behavior under previously unseen instructions.

The framework uses hierarchical imitation learning and vector quantization to learn discrete skill codes. These codes are strongly correlated with both language instructions and the learned policy’s behavior. That connection gives the skill representation an interpretable role: it links what an instruction expresses to the behavior the policy carries out.

In navigation and robotic manipulation environments, LISA outperforms a strong non-hierarchical baseline when training data are limited. It also composes learned skills to solve tasks involving unseen long-range instructions. These results support using a discrete intermediate skill layer to connect language and sequential decisions. The demonstrated value is both improved generalization in the studied settings and behavior that can be understood and controlled through learned skills.
neurips-2022-lisa-learning-interpretable.tldr: LISA learns interpretable discrete skills from language-conditioned demonstrations and composes them for unseen long-range instructions.

paragraphs: Forecasting physical dynamics becomes difficult when a model encounters different system parameters, external forces, or boundary conditions. DyAd addresses this variation by treating heterogeneous domains as different tasks. It aims to learn shared dynamics while adapting its forecasts to the hidden characteristics of a particular task.

The model has an encoder and a forecaster. With weak supervision, the encoder infers time-invariant task features. During inference, those features control the forecaster through adaptive instance normalization and adaptive padding. This division separates the task-specific information from the shared dynamics model, giving the forecaster a mechanism for responding to different physical settings.

The theoretical analysis relates generalization error to task relatedness within the source domain and differences between source and target domains. Thus, the result explicitly connects transfer performance to how the domains relate. Experiments report improvements over state-of-the-art approaches for turbulent flow, real-world sea surface temperature, and ocean currents. These findings support task inference as a useful basis for adapting dynamics forecasts.
neurips-2022-meta-learning-dynamics-fore.tldr: DyAd infers hidden task features to adapt a shared dynamics forecaster across heterogeneous physical domains.

paragraphs: Scientific uncertainty estimation often requires sampling from a density whose evaluation involves an expensive simulation, integral, or iterative calculation. Repeating that work at every Markov chain Monte Carlo step can be impractical. Cheaper approximations save computation but can bias the density being sampled.

The paper develops asymptotically exact multi-fidelity algorithms for settings with an available sequence of increasingly accurate models approximating the target density. It constructs a cheaper unbiased estimator by randomly truncating a telescoping series built from that sequence. A pseudo-marginal MCMC method then uses this randomized-fidelity estimator for inference.

The key distinction is between approximating individual computations and changing the eventual sampling target. The proposed construction supports asymptotic exactness while using models of varying fidelity; it does not claim finite-run exactness. The authors discuss and evaluate applications to log-Gaussian Cox processes, Bayesian identification of ordinary differential equation systems, optimization constrained by partial differential equations, and Gaussian process parameter inference. These examples span several sources of expensive density evaluations.
neurips-2022-multi-fidelity-monte-carlo-.tldr: Randomized combinations of increasingly accurate models enable asymptotically exact MCMC with cheaper unbiased density estimates.

paragraphs: Does the distribution used to initialize a neural network matter when the network becomes wide? This paper shows that the answer depends on which parameter tensors are being initialized. Some, described as matrix-like parameters, retain sensitivity to the initialization distribution, while others do not in the wide-network limit.

The authors develop a theory of non-Gaussian Tensor Programs to make this distinction precise. Their universality principle identifies when a program’s limiting behavior depends on the distributions of its initial matrices and vectors. The contribution therefore goes beyond comparing a few initialization choices: it provides a framework for determining when distributional details survive in the limit.

As consequences, the paper extends previous results from the Tensor Programs framework to networks with non-Gaussian weights. These include neural network Gaussian process and neural tangent kernel correspondence, the Free Independence Principle, the Dynamical Dichotomy Theorem, and mu-parametrization. The findings broaden the theory’s reach while preserving the distinction between parameters whose initialization distribution matters and those whose limiting behavior is universal.
neurips-2022-non-gaussian-tensor-program.tldr: Non-Gaussian Tensor Programs characterize when wide-network limits depend on the distributions used to initialize parameters.

paragraphs: Multi-task reinforcement learning seeks a policy that handles several tasks. Sharing parameters can exploit similarities among those tasks, but differences in their content and difficulty complicate the choice of what to share. Shared parameters also introduce optimization challenges because learning must accommodate multiple tasks at once.

PaCo approaches this through parameter composition. It learns a policy subspace represented by a set of parameters, with each individual task’s policy lying within that subspace. Task policies are formed by interpolating the learned parameter set. This provides a common learned foundation while allowing different tasks to use different compositions of it.

The authors present this construction as a way to make parameter sharing flexible and to improve training. They report state-of-the-art results on Meta-World benchmarks, supporting the effectiveness of the approach in those evaluations. The central idea is to make the relationship among task policies explicit through their shared parameter subspace, so that sharing and task-specific variation are represented together.
neurips-2022-paco-parameter-compositiona.tldr: PaCo learns a shared parameter subspace and constructs task policies by interpolation to enable flexible multi-task learning.

paragraphs: Variational autoencoders have inspired many model variants designed for different tasks. That variety makes a common implementation framework valuable for using and comparing them. Pythae is an open-source Python library that brings generative autoencoders together through unified implementations and a dedicated framework for reproducible, reliable use.

The paper also demonstrates the library through a benchmarking case study involving 19 generative autoencoder models. These models represent several major directions of improvement in the field. The comparison spans image reconstruction, generation, classification, clustering, and interpolation, examining the models across several uses of their learned representations.

This breadth matters because the case study treats autoencoders as tools for multiple downstream tasks, rather than evaluating only their ability to generate images. The contribution combines reusable software with a concrete comparative study built on it. The abstract presents the library and benchmark as the main results, providing a shared foundation for studying model variants and their behavior across these different tasks.
neurips-2022-pythae-unifying-generative-.tldr: Pythae unifies generative autoencoder implementations and demonstrates their comparison through a 19-model benchmark across five tasks.

paragraphs: Large web datasets have supported strong image-text models, but the effect of dataset construction on robustness remains less understood. This paper introduces a testbed using six sources: YFCC, LAION, Conceptual Captions, WIT, RedCaps, and Shutterstock. It studies how CLIP’s pretraining distribution affects performance under distribution shifts.

The experiments find substantial differences among data sources, with no source leading across every shift. Combining sources does not necessarily improve robustness and can dilute the robustness of the strongest individual source. This makes dataset composition a consequential choice: adding more data can change the properties that made a particular source effective.

A simplified theoretical setting also exhibits diluted robustness when training data are combined. The theory additionally offers a candidate explanation for the success of CLIP-based filtering used in LAION. Together, the empirical and theoretical results challenge the idea that collecting more web data is by itself the most effective route to robust generalization. They motivate closer attention to which data are combined and selected.
neurips-2022-quality-not-quantity-on-the.tldr: CLIP robustness depends strongly on pretraining data composition, and mixing sources can dilute the strongest source’s robustness.

paragraphs: SAPD+ addresses minimax optimization, where one set of variables is minimized while another is maximized. The studied objective combines closed convex terms with a smooth interaction that is weakly convex in the minimizing variables and concave or strongly concave in the maximizing variables. These assumptions define the scope of its guarantees.

The method achieves reported best-known stochastic oracle complexities of O(L κ_y ε^-4) for the strongly concave setting and O(L³ ε^-6) for the merely concave setting. Here, L is a Lipschitz constant and κ_y is the condition number. The guarantees do not require a compact problem domain, so that particular restriction is absent from the analysis.

A variance-reduced version achieves reported best-known complexity O(L κ_y² ε^-3) in the weakly convex–strongly concave setting. These bounds describe how oracle requirements scale with accuracy and problem properties. The authors also demonstrate efficiency on distributionally robust learning with a nonconvex regularizer and on deep-learning multiclass classification, pairing the complexity results with applied evaluations.
neurips-2022-sapd-an-accelerated-stochas.tldr: SAPD+ achieves best-known stated oracle complexities for specified nonconvex-concave minimax problems without requiring compact domains.

paragraphs: Annealed importance sampling estimates marginal likelihoods by moving through distributions that connect a tractable starting point to a target. A changing Markov chain approximately follows this sequence. An extended target distribution then supplies the reweighting needed to turn the sampled trajectory into an importance-sampling estimate.

Much work has improved the proposal by changing intermediate distributions or Markov transitions. This paper focuses on another component: the extended target used for reweighting is convenient but suboptimal, which can impair performance. The authors use ideas from score-based generative modeling to approximate the optimal extended target for proposals obtained by discretizing Langevin and Hamiltonian dynamics.

This gives differentiable AIS procedures that change how a proposal trajectory is evaluated through its extended target. The paper demonstrates them on synthetic benchmark distributions and variational autoencoders. Its contribution is to identify and address an underused design choice in AIS, connecting score-based modeling to marginal-likelihood estimation through improved approximation of the target used for reweighting.
neurips-2022-score-based-diffusion-meets.tldr: Score-based modeling approximates better extended targets for annealed importance sampling with Langevin and Hamiltonian proposals.

paragraphs: Recognizing an action from only a few example videos depends on matching spatial and temporal features reliably. Complex scenes and variable motion can make that alignment difficult. SST addresses both the representations extracted from videos and the way a query video is compared with its support examples.

First, the method searches for a video-specific transformer architecture that organizes spatial and temporal attention to produce stronger features. Second, it uses an efficient non-parametric alignment strategy. For every query and candidate category, it creates a query-specific class prototype, allowing the comparison to account for the particular sequence being recognized and all available support sequences.

The authors report substantial advantages on UCF101 and HMDB51. In the UCF101 five-way, one-shot setting without pretraining, they report a 17.1% top-one accuracy improvement over TRX with threefold fewer FLOPs. These findings support combining architecture design with query-dependent alignment: better features and more tailored comparisons jointly address the variability that makes recognition from very few examples difficult.
neurips-2022-searching-for-better-spatio.tldr: SST combines video-transformer architecture search with query-specific prototype alignment to improve few-shot action recognition.

paragraphs: Similarity graphs support clustering, classification, graph learning, and nearest-neighbor search, but dense graphs become impractical for massive datasets. Sparsity matters both when building the graph and when running later algorithms on it. Stars aims to preserve useful neighborhood structure while greatly reducing edges and expensive similarity comparisons.

The method builds two-hop spanners: graphs in which similar points can connect through a path of at most two edges. This allows an indirect connection to represent useful proximity. The theoretical result gives nearly linear construction time and places approximate nearest neighbors within two-hop neighborhoods, connecting the sparse structure to the information downstream tasks need.

The authors report deployments with hundreds of billions of nodes and tens of trillions of edges. Evaluations on clustering and graph learning show 10- to 1,000-fold improvements in pairwise similarity comparisons, substantial runtime gains, and negligible quality loss. These results indicate that preserving short paths between related points can make enormous similarity graphs useful without requiring dense direct connections.
neurips-2022-stars-tera-scale-graph-buil.tldr: Stars builds extremely sparse similarity graphs using two-hop connections, enabling massive-scale construction with far fewer comparisons.
